message:
Process completed with exit code 143.
  ##[error]The runner has received a shutdown signal.

11 MB of disk consumed across the whole 4.5-minute export with 88 GB still
free, against 2.3 GB -> 18.8 GB of committed memory still climbing at ~2 GB
per 30s when the runner was taken down. `dind-full` recorded the identical
curve 22 minutes earlier. So every reclaim on this branch so far was aimed at
the wrong resource: these jobs run out of memory, not disk.

dockerd buffering an export in anonymous memory is docker/buildx#1606, open
against the docker driver since Docker 23.0, with no daemon setting to turn it
off. What changed on our side is what gets exported: the same two jobs passed
on 2026-09-05 (run 33962512941, `exporting layers 171.1s done`) on the same
runner image and Docker 28.0.4, and commit 46f80a5 then made the Lean boxes
install a real toolchain, so the full box's `COPY --from=lean-stage
/home/box/.elan` stopped copying a stub.

16 GB of RAM is what an ubuntu-24.04 runner has and larger runners are not
available here, so scripts/ci/ensure-swap.sh converts the disk the measurement
shows sitting idle into the resource that ran out: a 32 GB total swap target,
29697 MB of it as a swapfile on /, sized down from the target only if it would
encroach on the 40 GB reserve the chain and its export still need. It decides
out loud on `[ensure-swap]` lines, `plan` mode prints the decision without
touching anything, `sudo -n` means a machine that would prompt fails instantly
instead of hanging, and failing to provision is a warning rather than a job
failure - the failure belongs on the build, whose log now explains itself.

pr-test-dind's `full` variant gets 90 minutes instead of 60: it reaches the
export ~37 minutes in and now spends that export paging, and a build killed
while it is making progress reports a timeout instead of the fix.

The sampler also names the biggest processes by resident memory now, because
"memory ran out" and "this process took it" are different findings and only
the second one points at anything - the daemon doing the export runs outside
the step's own process tree.

experiments/test-issue119-ci-resource-headroom.sh grows from 14 to 40
assertions: the sizing arithmetic and the reserve guard through `plan` mode,
and the sequence - allocate, format, enable, retry with dd when swapon refuses
a preallocated file, clean up what could not be enabled, recognise its own
swapfile on a second call - against stubs, because provisioning needs root and
a test that needs root is a test that does not run. Verified to fail on the
pre-fix tree in a scratch worktree, both for the missing script and for the
missing wiring.",
